score_scale.meaning: Higher is better for all score fields. For risk-related fields, higher means lower risk and better suitability.

hard_reject_conditions.logic: Reject if trademark, patent, design, copyright, fake brand, or misleading compatibility risk is high.
Reject if product requires certification, category approval, dangerous goods handling, medical or safety claims that the team cannot support.
Reject if estimated contribution margin after fulfillment, return cost, platform fee, and advertising is negative.
Reject for Amazon-first candidates if product is oversized, too heavy, fragile, restricted, hazardous, or likely to create unacceptable FBA cost.

Reject or hold for independent-site candidates if product claims, pricing, shipping, return policy, contact information, or landing page transparency cannot satisfy Google Merchant Center requirements.
Reject if return drivers are inherent to the product and cannot be reduced by design, instruction, packaging, sizing, or positioning.
Reject if the only viable strategy is lower price and there is no meaningful product, bundle, content, supply-chain, B2B, or brand differentiation.

demand_score.description: Measures whether real demand exists across marketplace, search, trend, and social signals.
inputs: Product Opportunity Explorer or niche demand signals

scoring_logic.90_100: Stable multi-source demand across Amazon, Google, and user communities.
scoring_logic.75_89: Strong demand in one main channel and supporting signals in at least one other channel.
scoring_logic.60_74: Demand exists but is narrow, seasonal, or not yet well cross-validated.
scoring_logic.0_59: Demand is weak, short-lived, unproven, or based on one unreliable signal.

competition_score.description: Measures whether the candidate can realistically enter the market. Higher score means easier competition.
inputs: SERP authority for independent site keywords

scoring_logic.90_100: Competitors are fragmented, listing/content quality gaps exist, and no dominant review wall blocks entry.
scoring_logic.75_89: Competition is meaningful but there are visible weak points or long-tail entry paths.
scoring_logic.60_74: Entry is possible only with clear differentiation or supply-chain advantage.
scoring_logic.0_59: Market is dominated by strong brands, high reviews, low prices, high CPC, or high-authority SERPs.

profit_score.description: Measures contribution profit after real selling costs.
inputs: FBA fee or independent-site fulfillment cost
profit_score.amazon_formula: target_price - COGS - first_mile - FBA_fee - referral_fee - storage_estimate - return_cost - coupon - PPC_cost_per_order
profit_score.independent_site_formula: AOV * gross_margin - CPC / conversion_rate - shipping_subsidy - payment_fee - return_cost - allocated_content_or_creator_cost

scoring_logic.90_100: Healthy contribution margin after conservative ad and return assumptions.
scoring_logic.75_89: Profitable with manageable sensitivity to CPC, return rate, or discounting.
scoring_logic.60_74: Thin but possible if conversion or sourcing improves.
scoring_logic.0_59: Contribution margin is too thin, fragile, or negative.

differentiation_score.description: Measures whether the product can be improved, bundled, contentized, customized, or branded.

scoring_logic.90_100: Clear fixable pain points and multiple factory-feasible differentiation paths.
scoring_logic.75_89: At least one strong product or bundle improvement path exists.
scoring_logic.60_74: Differentiation is possible but not yet proven.
scoring_logic.0_59: Product can only compete on price, color, or generic copy.

compliance_risk_score.description: Measures whether compliance, policy, category, IP, and fulfillment risks are acceptable. Higher score means lower risk.

scoring_logic.90_100: Low-risk ordinary product with no obvious policy, certification, or IP barrier.
scoring_logic.75_89: Some checks required but risks are manageable with documentation.
scoring_logic.60_74: Moderate risk, requires manual review before testing.
scoring_logic.0_59: High risk or unclear compliance path; hold or reject.

scoring_logic.90_100: Strong long-tail clusters with commercial intent and content-to-product fit.
scoring_logic.75_89: Good SEO opportunity with moderate difficulty.
scoring_logic.60_74: SEO can support but should not be the main channel.
scoring_logic.0_59: Little search demand or no content-to-product conversion path.

ads_score.description: Measures whether paid acquisition is economically realistic.

scoring_logic.90_100: High commercial intent, manageable CPC, high margin, strong conversion path.
scoring_logic.75_89: Paid testing is reasonable with a controlled budget.
scoring_logic.60_74: Ads can be used only for validation or retargeting.
scoring_logic.0_59: Paid traffic likely destroys margin or triggers policy risk.

b2b_score.description: Measures wholesale, inquiry, customization, and factory-led sales potential.
inputs: spec sheet or case study potential

scoring_logic.90_100: Strong industry use case, customization, bulk purchase, and RFQ path.
scoring_logic.60_74: B2B may exist but needs validation.
scoring_logic.0_59: Mostly consumer one-off purchase with little inquiry value.

brandability_score.description: Measures whether the product can become a brand asset rather than a one-off SKU.

scoring_logic.90_100: Clear audience, repeat or ecosystem potential, and strong story or visual identity.
scoring_logic.75_89: Can support brand pages and product series.
scoring_logic.60_74: Some brand value but mostly transactional.
scoring_logic.0_59: Generic commodity with weak memory and low loyalty.

automation_fit_score.description: Measures whether the product can feed Barong's downstream K/I/P/GMC/SEO automation systems.

scoring_logic.90_100: Ready to hand off to K/I/P/GMC/SEO with structured assets.
scoring_logic.60_74: Some downstream work can begin after missing fields are filled.
scoring_logic.0_59: Too vague or unstructured for automation.

final_score_formula: weighted_average(demand_score, competition_score, profit_score, differentiation_score, compliance_risk_score, seo_score, ads_score, b2b_score, brandability_score, automation_fit_score)

priority_test.condition: final_score >= 85 and no hard_reject_conditions are true
priority_test.action: Enter sample, small-batch, landing page, or ad validation immediately.

test_after_review.condition: final_score >= 75 and final_score < 85 and no hard_reject_conditions are true
test_after_review.action: Proceed after manual review of weakest dimensions.

watchlist.condition: final_score >= 65 and final_score < 75 and no hard_reject_conditions are true
watchlist.action: Keep in research pool; monitor trend, competition, sourcing, or content signals.

reject_for_now.condition: final_score >= 50 and final_score < 65 and no hard_reject_conditions are true
reject_for_now.action: Do not develop now unless a special supply-chain or customer advantage appears.

hard_reject.action: Reject regardless of total score unless owner explicitly approves a compliance or legal review path.

amazon_first.condition: Amazon demand is strong, FBA and profit are viable, competition is enterable, and independent-site score is not yet strong.

site_first.condition: SEO, B2B, content, customization, or inquiry potential is strong, while Amazon is weak or not suitable for standardized SKU launch.
handoff: GMC readiness review if product can be listed

dual_channel.condition: Amazon score and independent-site score are both strong and compliance risk is low.

barong_weight_bias.description: For Barong Yekhna, prioritize products that are differentiable, content-friendly, factory-controllable, and suitable for downstream automation.
boost_conditions: SEO and content map are strong
B2B customization or inquiry potential exists
